title: Teena Sehgal v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
coram: Shekhar B. Saraf, J. & Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary, J.
disposition: Writ petition disposed of; connection to be given on part-payment of dues and an indemnity bond
headnote: An occupier of a distinct portion of premises (here a daughter-in-law residing on the ground floor, in dispute with her mother-in-law who has shifted to solar power) is entitled to a new domestic electricity connection, but cannot obtain it without paying the electricity dues attributable to that portion. With about Rs. 2.41 lakh pending for the whole premises, the Court fixed the ground-floor liability at Rs. 1,20,000 and directed the petitioner to pay 50% within two weeks and the balance in four monthly instalments, to furnish an Indemnity Bond (Annexure 4.2 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005) for her ground-floor residence, and to pay regular bills; on the 50% payment the authority must provide the new connection on completion of formalities.

holding_units.topic: Occupier's connection on an indemnity bond, conditioned on clearing the portion's dues
holding_units.question: Can an occupier of part of a premises get a new connection despite an owner-occupier dispute and outstanding dues on the whole premises?
holding_units.holding: Yes, on conditions. The petitioner residing on the ground floor (undisputed) is entitled to a connection, but not without paying the dues attributable to that portion. The Court fixed the ground-floor liability at Rs. 1,20,000 (50% in two weeks, balance in four instalments), required an Indemnity Bond (Annexure 4.2) for her ground-floor residence and payment of regular bills, and directed the authority to provide the new connection on the 50% payment and completion of formalities.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Owner-occupier (mother-in-law/daughter-in-law) dispute with a pending civil suit; mother-in-law on the first floor shifted to solar; about Rs. 2.41 lakh pending for the entire premises.

principle_tags.application: An occupier of a distinct portion may obtain a connection on an Indemnity Bond (Annexure 4.2) despite an owner-occupier dispute, subject to clearing the dues attributable to that portion.
A new connection to a portion of premises is conditioned on payment of the electricity dues attributable to that portion; dues on the premises must be cleared before supply.

not_decided.point: The owner-occupier civil dispute and the exact apportionment of dues
not_decided.note: The civil suit between the parties is pending; the Court fixed the ground-floor liability pragmatically at Rs. 1,20,000 without finally adjudicating the apportionment of the total Rs. 2.41 lakh.
